title: Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets
description:
# Partition to K Equal Sum Subsets

Given an integer array `nums` and an integer `k`, return `true` if it is possible to split every element of `nums` into exactly `k` non-empty subsets whose sums are all equal.

Every element must belong to exactly one subset. Subsets need not be contiguous; do not omit or reuse elements.

## Example 1:

**Input:** nums = [4,3,2,3,5,2,1], k = 4
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** One valid partition is `[5]`, `[1,4]`, `[2,3]`, and `[2,3]`. Each subset sums to `5`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** nums = [1,2,3,4], k = 3
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** The total sum is `10`, which is not divisible by `3`.

## Constraints:

* `1 <= k <= nums.length <= 16`
* `1 <= nums[i] <= 10^4`
* The frequency of each element is in the range `[1, 4]`.

solutions.name: Bucket Sums with Symmetry Pruning
solutions.description:
## Approach

First compute the total sum. If it is not divisible by `k`, no equal partition is possible. Sort the array so larger numbers are placed first, then recursively assign the next number to one of the `k` bucket sums without exceeding the target. At each recursion level, skip buckets that currently have the same sum because placing the number into either bucket would create equivalent states.

## Key Insight

The subsets have no labels. Two empty buckets, or two buckets with the same current sum, are interchangeable. Symmetry pruning is what keeps direct bucket assignment from repeating the same search under different bucket names.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(k^n) in the worst case because each element may try several buckets
- Space Complexity: O(k + n), for bucket sums plus recursion depth

solutions.name: Build One Target Subset at a Time
solutions.description:
## Approach

Sort the numbers and repeatedly build one subset whose sum is the target. A `used` array marks numbers that already belong to completed subsets. When the current subset reaches the target, start building the next subset from the largest unused number. Duplicate values and failed empty-subset starts are skipped to avoid equivalent branches.

## Key Insight

Instead of assigning every number to a named bucket, this route treats all completed buckets as identical and only searches for the next target-sum subset. When only one bucket remains, the remaining numbers must sum to the target, so the recursion can return true immediately.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(k * 2^n * n) in the worst case, because many unused masks may be explored while forming each target subset
- Space Complexity: O(n), for the `used` array and recursion depth

solutions.name: Bottom-Up Bitmask DP
solutions.description:
## Approach

Represent the set of already used numbers with a bit mask. `dp[mask]` stores the current partial bucket sum modulo the target for reachable masks, or `-1` when the mask is unreachable. From each reachable mask, try adding one unused number if it does not overflow the current bucket.

## Key Insight

The modulo value is enough state: whenever the partial sum becomes `0`, one bucket has just been completed. If the full mask is reachable with modulo `0`, then all numbers can be arranged into complete target-sum buckets.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^n), because each mask tries up to `n` next elements
- Space Complexity: O(2^n), for the reachable-mask table

solutions.name: Top-Down Memoized Remaining Mask
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a mask of unused numbers and recursively choose one number to add to the current bucket. The current bucket sum is carried modulo the target. Failed states are memoized by `unusedMask` when starting a new bucket, which is the point where bucket identities no longer matter.

## Key Insight

A remaining mask fully describes the future search whenever the current bucket is empty. Memoizing those boundary states prevents the algorithm from rebuilding the same set of remaining buckets through different earlier choices.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n * 2^n), because each remaining mask may scan the available bits
- Space Complexity: O(2^n), for memoized masks plus recursion depth
